clue.text: Imagist dispensed with act — lacking ability to focus

indicators.note: dispensed means handed out or scattered, so the letters of both words are distributed into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet of the Imagist school does away with an act on stage and loses focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispensed with' reads as 'did without', but 'dispensed' is the anagram signal and 'with' only joins IMAGIST and ACT, whose ten letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An astigmatic eye has a defect of curvature that stops it bringing light to a sharp focus.

clue.text: Getting to be in need of a prompt reaction to drought?

definitions.text: Getting to be in need of a prompt
definitions.meaning: an actor who forgets their lines on stage and needs the prompter's help
what rivers and reservoirs do when no rain falls

explanation.definitionFit: Theatre slang for forgetting one's lines, and the literal sense of water sources shrinking away in dry weather.

clue.text: Well set fashion house event

parts.note: a well or spring is a source of water from the ground
a set of things is a collection of them

explanation.surface: A carefully arranged show staged by a couture firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well set' looks like a phrase meaning neatly arranged; split it into two synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashion houses unveil each season's range of new designs at a catwalk show, such as the one shown for spring.

clue.text: The biggest of the canvas carriers (medium) is not commonly found round mother's

definitions.text: The biggest of the canvas carriers

parts.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

indicators.note: found round says one piece sits around another, so one word is placed outside the other

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of is not
ma is mother, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Something medium-sized is rarely seen near mum's sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The canvas is the sails, so the canvas carriers are the masts of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship the principal and tallest mast, which bears the largest sails, has this name.

clue.text: See 3
Uppity head, one interrupting house's exuberant friendliness

indicators.note: in a down clue uppity, going upward, means the word head is written bottom to top

parts.note: nob is slang for the head

indicators.note: interrupting means one piece breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: a house is a home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A self-important boss barges into a household full of good cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Uppity' means read upward; 'interrupting' signals a container. Nob is old slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is a cheerful, good-natured warmth towards others, a genial sociability.

clue.text: Debut of Bernard "Leaving the Country" Manning, perhaps

indicators.note: leaving means the letter goes away from the word, so it is removed

parts.note: Bolivia is a country in South America

indicators.note: the debut is the first appearance, so take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Bernard Manning, the comedian, makes his first appearance with a routine called Leaving the Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Bernard Manning was a British stand-up comedian; the definition is another Manning, the novelist Olivia Manning, author of the Balkan Trilogy.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivia Manning was an English novelist, so her forename is an example of a Manning by first name.

clue.text: Foil the closing of valve to make water

indicators.note: the closing of a word is its final letter, so take the end of valve

parts.note: to make water is to urinate, to pee

explanation.surface: A plumbing instruction: shut the valve to get the water flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' looks like a verb meaning thwart, but it is the light fencing sword.
explanation.definitionFit: The foil and this sword are both weapons used in the sport of fencing, so one stands as an example of the other.

clue.text: Party whip takes lead, grabbing secretary for excruciating punishment

indicators.note: grabbing means one piece holds another within it
the whip takes the lead, so its word goes in front of the party

parts.note: a strap is a leather whip
a do is a party
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A party's chief whip takes charge and hauls in a secretary for a harsh reprimand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party whip' suggests a parliamentary whip, but the two words are separate pieces, and 'takes lead' tells you the whip goes in front of the party before 'grabbing' takes the secretary in.
explanation.definitionFit: The strappado was a torture in which the victim was hoisted by a rope tied to the wrists and dropped.

clue.text: Runs during game, back lower deck

indicators.note: back here means the whole assembled piece is read in the reverse direction
during means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Points scored while a match is underway, then a return below decks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts R inside POLO to make POLRO, and 'back' reverses all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship, below the waterline.

clue.text: Former dictator in the Middle Eastern Republic of Iris

indicators.note: in means the dictator is placed inside the country

parts.note: Iran is an Islamic republic in the Middle East
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda in the 1970s

explanation.surface: An ex-tyrant turns up in a Middle Eastern state named after a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Iris' looks like part of a country's name, but it is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes things relating to the iris, whether of the eye or the rainbow goddess.

clue.text: Port getting Ravel drunk when he composed inside

indicators.note: inside means the second piece is put within the first
drunk means disordered, so the letters of Ravel are jumbled
composed means put together or arranged, so the two letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ravel, the French composer, gets drunk in a harbour town while writing music.
explanation.walkthrough: Maurice Ravel was a French composer, which makes 'composed' look like part of the story; it is a second anagram signal, beside 'drunk', and 'inside' sets one result (LAVRE, EH) within the other.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major seaport in Normandy, at the mouth of the Seine.

clue.text: One of a biblical pair, mother to the first

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
of the biblical pair named in Ezekiel and Revelation, the first named is Gog

explanation.surface: A Bible reference to twin figures, with a mother attached to the elder.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair is Gog and Magog, so 'the first' of them gives the other name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gog and Magog appear together in the Bible as enemies of God's people; this is the second of the two.

clue.text: Go round and measure, say, Araucaria's top half, fool!

parts.note: an en is a printers' measure of width, one example of a measure

indicators.note: top half means only the first half of the word is kept, so the second half is dropped

parts.note: Araucaria was a famous crossword compiler for this newspaper
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and measure the upper part of a monkey-puzzle tree, you idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria is the monkey-puzzle tree, but here it is the pseudonym of the setter John Graham; he was a COMPILER, and 'top half' keeps COMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass is to surround or encircle something.

clue.text: See 21
He keeps a much less mature person shifting 500 drugs a day

definitions.text: He keeps a much less mature person

indicators.note: shifting means moving the letters about into a new order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone moving large quantities of drugs every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' means supports financially, the way a rich older lover keeps a young partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar daddy is a wealthy older man who lavishes gifts on a much younger lover.

clue.text: There's a lot more, in fact, in the main car:- female article; gems; and black work unit

definitions.text: There's a lot more, in fact, in the main

parts.note: the Tipo is a model of Fiat car
the is the definite article
ice is slang for diamonds
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an erg is a unit of work or energy in physics

explanation.surface: A shopping list of a car, a woman, an article, jewels and a black item, with much more hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the open sea, where an iceberg shows only a small part above the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the small visible part of a much larger problem, as most of an iceberg lies under the sea.

clue.text: Wildness is terribly erotic in farm yard entrances

indicators.note: in means the rearranged word sits between the two letters
entrances are where you go in, so the first letters of the words
terribly means badly, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unrestrained passion breaks out by the gates of a farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrances' looks like doorways of the farmyard but means the opening letters of farm and yard; 'terribly' scrambles to EROCIT, set 'in' them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferocity is savage fierceness, the wildness of an untamed creature.

clue.text: Dignified death, clutching gold piece

indicators.note: clutching means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: end is a word for death
a noble was an old English gold coin

explanation.surface: A stately death, the dying hand gripping a gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ennobled is to be raised to the nobility, or more loosely made dignified and elevated.

clue.text: Show-off outdoor singer: "Key indicator of Mozart work in con brio version"

indicators.note: in means the two letters are placed inside the rearranged phrase
a version is a new rendering, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is a musical key
K, for Köchel, prefixes the catalogue numbers of Mozart's works

explanation.surface: Advice on how to play a vigorous Mozart piece, with key and catalogue number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' turns CON BRIO into COROBIN; 'in' places CK after the CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock robin is a male robin, a garden songbird that sings outdoors and displays boldly.

clue.text: Yellow informer

definitions.meaning: a bright pale shade named after a songbird
criminal slang for someone who sings to the police

explanation.definitionFit: A bright yellow is named after the songbird, and an informer is said to sing, hence the slang.

clue.text: Ship's aid (Issue One) with reverse

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
a is the article meaning one
R is the abbreviation for reverse, as on a gear stick

explanation.surface: A navigation device fitted to a vessel, with issues over going astern.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar is sound-based echo detection, used by ships to find depth and underwater objects.

clue.text: One who reckons showing off is an arty academic event

parts.note: a summer is one who sums, adding up figures
an exhibition is a display of showing off

explanation.surface: A pompous calculating type parading as an art-world figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Academy in London holds an annual open art show of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Academy's annual open art show in London is its best-known event.

clue.text: Crew cross short sailing boat to see creature coming to a perfunctory end

definitions.text: creature coming to a perfunctory end

parts.note: to man is to crew a vessel
X is a cross shape
cat is short for catamaran, a twin-hulled sailing boat

explanation.surface: Sailors crossing to a small boat spot an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfunctory end' is a joke on the tailless cat from the Isle of Man: its end is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of domestic cat from the Isle of Man is born with no tail, hence its abrupt rear.

clue.text: See 4
"Country mania" is touring round in the same place

indicators.note: round means the jumbled word goes around the abbreviation
touring means travelling about, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: ib. is short for ibidem, Latin for in the same place

explanation.surface: Travel fever grips a nation, staying put all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Country mania' look like a title; 'Country' is the definition. 'touring' scrambles the other word to NAMIA, and 'round' wraps it around ib., the footnote abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a country in south-western Africa, an example of a nation state.

clue.text: To an unholy alliance

indicators.note: unholy means wicked or dreadful, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A toast to a wicked pact.
explanation.definitionFit: This military alliance of North American and European nations was founded in 1949.

clue.text: Fish river in a row

indicators.note: in means the letter is put inside the word

parts.note: a spat is a row or quarrel

explanation.surface: Fishing on a river, sitting in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small silvery fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Relating to those people with objective healing

parts.note: on means about or relating to
them refers to those people
an end is an objective or aim

explanation.surface: A description of people with a goal in recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone recovering from illness or injury is said to be getting better in this phrase.
